  note: >-

## formal
Let $\Cl(\ell,\ell)$ be the algebra of $\ell$ modes of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.mode-split-of-the-clifford-algebra-and-its-klein-twist-to-the-tensor-product}: generators $e_{k}$, $f_{k}$ with $Q(e_{k}) = 1$, $Q(f_{k}) = -1$, mode parities $p_{k} = f_{k}e_{k}$, $\Gamma_{X} = \prod_{k \in X}p_{k}$, total parity $\Gamma$, the anti-automorphism $\dagger$ fixing each $e_{k}$ and negating each $f_{k}$, coefficients in $\Q$ or any ordered field. An \emph{observable} is an $x$ with $x^{\dagger} = x$, $x^{2} = 1$; it is \emph{even} if $\Gamma x = x\Gamma$. A \emph{state} is a linear functional $\varphi$ with $\varphi(1) = 1$, $\varphi(xx^{\dagger}) \ge 0$; it is even if $\varphi(\Gamma x\Gamma) = \varphi(x)$. For disjoint sets of modes $A$, $B$ and observables $A_{1}, A_{2}$, $B_{1}, B_{2}$ with $A_{i}B_{j} = B_{j}A_{i}$, put $C = A_{1}B_{1} + A_{1}B_{2} + A_{2}B_{1} - A_{2}B_{2}$; then $C^{2} = 4 - [A_{1},A_{2}][B_{1},B_{2}]$ and $\varphi(C)^{2} \le \varphi(C^{2})$ (classical; two lines, in the proof).
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Even observables need no twist; proved.)} Even elements of $\Cl(A)$ and of $\Cl(B)$ commute, and the even part of the twisted algebra $B'$ generated by the $y\Gamma_{A}$ is the even part of $\Cl(B)$, with $(y\Gamma_{A})(y'\Gamma_{A}) = yy'$ for generators $y, y'$ of $\Cl(B)$. So for even observables the graded split and the Klein-twisted split are the same split, and any even observables $A_{i} \in \Cl(A)$, $B_{j} \in \Cl(B)$ satisfy $A_{i}B_{j} = B_{j}A_{i}$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(One mode is not enough; proved.)} The self-adjoint elements of the algebra $\Cl(1,1)$ of one mode $k$ are $s + tp_{k} + ue_{k}$; its observables are $\pm 1$ and $tp_{k} + ue_{k}$ with $t^{2} + u^{2} = 1$; its even observables are $\pm 1$ and $\pm p_{k}$, which commute. Hence if one party's two observables are even elements of the algebra of a single mode, then $C^{2} = 4$ and $|\varphi(C)| \le 2$ for every state, whatever the other party, with or without the twist.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Two modes per party are enough; proved.)} For $\ell = 4$, $A = \{1,2\}$, $B = \{3,4\}$, the elements $A_{1} = p_{1}$, $A_{2} = e_{1}f_{2}$, $B_{1} = p_{3}$, $B_{2} = e_{3}f_{4}$ are even observables with $A_{1}A_{2} = -A_{2}A_{1}$, $B_{1}B_{2} = -B_{2}B_{1}$, and $C^{2} = 4 + 4K$, $K = -f_{1}f_{2}f_{3}f_{4}$, an even observable commuting with $C$. For $8r^{2} \le 1$ the functional $\varphi_{r}(x) = \langle(1 + K)(1 + rC)x\rangle_{0}$ is an even state with $\varphi_{r}(C) = 8r$ and $\varphi_{r}(C^{2}) = 8$: over $\Q$ the supremum $2\sqrt{2}$ is approached and not attained, and it is attained when $\sqrt{2}$ is a coefficient.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(The twisted split of one mode per party; proved.)} For $\ell = 2$, $A = \{1\}$, $B = \{2\}$, the observables $p_{1}, e_{1}$ of $\Cl(A)$ and $p_{2}, e_{2}p_{1}$ of $B'$ commute across the parties and anticommute within each. On the even pure state $\rho = \tfrac14(1 + p_{1}p_{2}) + \tfrac12(w_{1}w_{2} + v_{2}v_{1})$, the pair state of clause (v) of the stored theorem at equal weights, with value $\varphi(x) = 4\langle\rho x\rangle_{0}$: $\varphi(p_{1}p_{2}) = \varphi(e_{1}\,e_{2}p_{1}) = 1$, $\varphi(p_{1}\,e_{2}p_{1}) = \varphi(e_{1}p_{2}) = 0$, and with $B_{\pm} = cp_{2} \pm s\,e_{2}p_{1}$, $c^{2} + s^{2} = 1$, the CHSH element of $(p_{1}, e_{1}; B_{+}, B_{-})$ has value $2(c + s)$, above $2$ for $c, s > 0$ (for example $\tfrac{14}{5}$ at $(\tfrac35, \tfrac45)$). The observables $e_{1}$ and $e_{2}p_{1}$ are odd: they anticommute with $\Gamma$, and the parity average $E(x) = \tfrac12(x + \Gamma x\Gamma)$ of Theorem \claimref{singularity.descent-parity-average} (in its total-parity form) sends them to $0$; with every observable replaced by its parity average the value is $2c \le 2$. By (ii) no other choice of observables repairs this: a value above $2$ on one mode per party requires observables that are not even.
\item[(v)] \emph{(Without the twist; proved.)} $e_{1}$ and $e_{2}$ anticommute, $e_{1}e_{2}$ is anti-self-adjoint, and $\varphi(e_{1}e_{2}) = 0$ for every state with $\varphi(x^{\dagger}) = \varphi(x)$, in particular for every $\varphi = \langle\rho\,\cdot\,\rangle_{0}$ with $\rho^{\dagger} = \rho$. The self-adjoint part of the untwisted element $e_{1}e_{2} + e_{1}p_{2} + p_{1}e_{2} - p_{1}p_{2}$ is $H = e_{1}p_{2} + p_{1}e_{2} - p_{1}p_{2}$, with $H^{2} = 3$, so $\varphi(H)^{2} \le 3 < 4$ for every state.
\end{enumerate}

## technical
In the Clifford algebra of fermionic modes, odd elements of two disjoint sets of modes anticommute, and the stored Klein twist is what makes them commute. This result separates what the twist buys from what it does not. If the observables of a party are parity-even, the twist is idle: even elements of disjoint mode sets already commute and the twisted and untwisted even algebras coincide. With even observables a party holding one mode has only the parity itself, so every CHSH value is at most $2$; a party needs two modes, and with two modes each there are even observables with CHSH square $4 + 4K$ and even states with values $8r$ for all $8r^{2} \le 1$, of supremum $2\sqrt{2}$. On one mode per party the twisted split does give values $2(c + s)$ up to $2\sqrt{2}$ on the stored even pair state, but only through the observables $e_{1}$ and $e_{2}p_{1}$, which anticommute with the parity and which the stored parity average sends to zero. So the question whether a single entangled pair of modes shows a CHSH value above $2$ is the question whether parity-odd elements are observables, which is a choice of premise and is not settled here. Without the twist the odd-odd product has value zero in every state given by a self-adjoint element and the self-adjoint part of the CHSH expression has square $3$. All of this is classical (fermion parity superselection and the known need for two copies of a mode-entangled state); the statement in the series' algebra, with the stored twist and parity average, is what is recorded.

## lay
Two parties share particles of the kind that obey the exclusion principle, described by slots that are either empty or full. A long-standing rule says that nothing measurable can change the number of such particles from even to odd. If each party may only use measurements obeying that rule, then one shared slot each is not enough to show the quantum excess over the everyday limit of $2$: each party has only one such measurement, "is my slot full". Two slots each are enough, and then nothing special is needed to make the two parties' measurements compatible. A stored device called the Klein twist makes rule-breaking measurements of the two parties compatible, and with them one slot each does exceed $2$; whether such measurements exist is a choice this result leaves open. The mathematics is known; it is recorded here inside the series' algebra.

## one-liner
In the Clifford algebra of modes, parity-even observables of disjoint mode sets commute with no Klein twist; with them a one-mode party gives CHSH square $4$ (value at most $2$) and two modes per party give $C^{2} = 4 + 4K$ with even rational states of values $8r$, $8r^{2} \le 1$; the twisted one-mode split exceeds $2$ only through parity-odd observables, which the parity average erases.

proofs.proof-main.tex:
\emph{Preliminaries.} The blades are a basis, $e_{S}e_{S}^{\dagger} = 1$ and $\langle xy^{\dagger}\rangle_{0}$ is the sum of products of coefficients (the preliminaries of the proof of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.mode-split-of-the-clifford-algebra-and-its-klein-twist-to-the-tensor-product}); so $\langle xx^{\dagger}\rangle_{0} \ge 0$, $\langle ab\rangle_{0} = \langle ba\rangle_{0}$, and a self-adjoint blade has square $1$. For commuting pairs: $(A_{i}B_{j})^{\dagger} = B_{j}A_{i} = A_{i}B_{j}$, so $C^{\dagger} = C$; with $S = B_{1} + B_{2}$, $D = B_{1} - B_{2}$, $C = A_{1}S + A_{2}D$ and $C^{2} = S^{2} + D^{2} + A_{1}A_{2}SD + A_{2}A_{1}DS = 4 - [A_{1},A_{2}][B_{1},B_{2}]$, since $SD = -[B_{1},B_{2}] = -DS$. For a state, $0 \le \varphi((C - t)(C - t)^{\dagger})$ at $t = \varphi(C)$ gives $\varphi(C)^{2} \le \varphi(C^{2})$.

\emph{(i).} Clause (i) of the stored theorem gives $xy = (-1)^{|x||y|}yx$ for homogeneous $x \in \Cl(A)$, $y \in \Cl(B)$, so even elements commute. Clause (ii) gives $y\Gamma_{A}y'\Gamma_{A} = yy'$ for generators of $\Cl(B)$ and that the even part of $B'$ is the even part of $\Cl(B)$. An element of $\Cl(A)$ or of $\Cl(B)$ commutes with $\Gamma$ exactly when it is even, since $\Gamma$ anticommutes with every generator.

\emph{(ii).} The blades of the algebra of mode $k$ are $1$, $e_{k}$, $f_{k}$, $p_{k} = f_{k}e_{k}$; $f_{k}^{\dagger} = -f_{k}$ and $p_{k}^{\dagger} = e_{k}^{\dagger}f_{k}^{\dagger} = -e_{k}f_{k} = p_{k}$, so the self-adjoint elements are $s + tp_{k} + ue_{k}$. Since $p_{k}$ and $e_{k}$ anticommute and have square $1$, $(s + tp_{k} + ue_{k})^{2} = s^{2} + t^{2} + u^{2} + 2s(tp_{k} + ue_{k})$, which is $1$ exactly when $t = u = 0$, $s = \pm 1$, or $s = 0$, $t^{2} + u^{2} = 1$. The element is even exactly when $u = 0$. So the even observables are $\pm 1$, $\pm p_{k}$; they commute, $[A_{1},A_{2}] = 0$, $C^{2} = 4$ and $\varphi(C)^{2} \le 4$. Nothing was assumed about the other party beyond $A_{i}B_{j} = B_{j}A_{i}$.

\emph{(iii).} $e_{1}f_{2}$ is self-adjoint ($f_{2}^{\dagger}e_{1}^{\dagger} = -f_{2}e_{1} = e_{1}f_{2}$) with square $-e_{1}^{2}f_{2}^{2} = 1$, and it anticommutes with $p_{1} = f_{1}e_{1}$, which contains $e_{1}$ and not $f_{2}$; likewise for $B$. All four are products of two generators, hence even, and commute across the parties by (i). Then $[A_{1},A_{2}] = 2p_{1}e_{1}f_{2} = 2f_{1}f_{2}$, $[B_{1},B_{2}] = 2f_{3}f_{4}$ and $C^{2} = 4 - 4f_{1}f_{2}f_{3}f_{4} = 4 + 4K$. $K$ is a product of the commuting anti-self-adjoint elements $f_{1}f_{2}$, $f_{3}f_{4}$ of square $-1$, so $K^{\dagger} = K$, $K^{2} = 1$; it is even, and it commutes with each $A_{i}B_{j}$ because $A_{i}$ anticommutes with $A_{1}A_{2}$ and $B_{j}$ with $B_{1}B_{2}$. As the $A$'s commute with the $B$'s, $KA_{1}B_{1} = -(A_{1}A_{2}A_{1})(B_{1}B_{2}B_{1}) = -A_{2}B_{2}$, $KA_{2}B_{2} = -A_{1}B_{1}$, $KA_{1}B_{2} = A_{2}B_{1}$, $KA_{2}B_{1} = A_{1}B_{2}$, so $KC = C$ and $C^{3} = 8C$. The four terms of $C$ and $K$ are blades other than $1$, so $\langle C\rangle_{0} = \langle KC\rangle_{0} = \langle K\rangle_{0} = 0$, whence $\varphi_{r}(1) = 1$, $\varphi_{r}(C) = r\langle(1 + K)(4 + 4K)\rangle_{0} = 8r$ and $\varphi_{r}(C^{2}) = 8 + 8r\langle(1 + K)C\rangle_{0} = 8$. Positivity: with $P = \tfrac12(1 + K)$ and $y = Px$, $\tfrac12\varphi_{r}(xx^{\dagger}) = \langle y^{\dagger}y\rangle_{0} + r\langle y^{\dagger}Cy\rangle_{0}$, and by the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for the positive form $\langle a^{\dagger}b\rangle_{0}$, $\langle y^{\dagger}Cy\rangle_{0}^{2} \le \langle y^{\dagger}y\rangle_{0}\langle y^{\dagger}C^{2}y\rangle_{0} = 8\langle y^{\dagger}y\rangle_{0}^{2}$ (as $C^{2}P = 8P$); so $8r^{2} \le 1$ gives $\varphi_{r}(xx^{\dagger}) \ge 0$. The element $(1 + K)(1 + rC)$ is even, so $\varphi_{r}$ is even. The rational $r$ with $8r^{2} \le 1$ have supremum $\sqrt{2}/4$, not rational.

\emph{(iv).} By clause (ii) of the stored theorem $e_{2}p_{1}$ has square $1$ and commutes with $\Cl(A)$; it is self-adjoint since $e_{2}$ and $p_{1}$ are and commute; it anticommutes with $p_{2}$ as $e_{2}$ does; $p_{2}$ commutes with $\Cl(A)$. So the four elements are a CHSH configuration. The state is the pair state of clause (v) of the stored theorem with $c = s$, $r = 0$, there shown to be pure and even. Expanding the null vectors, $w_{1}w_{2} + v_{2}v_{1} = -\tfrac12(e_{1}f_{2} + f_{1}e_{2})$, so $\rho = \tfrac14(1 + p_{1}p_{2} - e_{1}f_{2} - f_{1}e_{2})$, a sum of four blades of square $1$. The value $4\langle\rho x\rangle_{0}$ of a blade $x$ of square $1$ is its coefficient in $4\rho$: it is $1$ for $p_{1}p_{2}$ and for $e_{1}\,e_{2}p_{1} = e_{2}f_{1} = -f_{1}e_{2}$, and $0$ for the odd blades $p_{1}\,e_{2}p_{1} = e_{2}$ and $e_{1}p_{2}$. With $B_{\pm} = cp_{2} \pm s\,e_{2}p_{1}$: $\varphi(C) = \varphi(p_{1}(B_{+} + B_{-})) + \varphi(e_{1}(B_{+} - B_{-})) = 2c\,\varphi(p_{1}p_{2}) + 2s\,\varphi(e_{1}e_{2}p_{1}) = 2(c + s)$, and $(c + s)^{2} = 1 + 2cs > 1$ for $c, s > 0$. $\Gamma$ anticommutes with every generator, so with $e_{1}$ and with $e_{2}p_{1}$ (three generators), and the parity average $E(x) = \tfrac12(x + \Gamma x\Gamma)$, which is the average of Theorem \claimref{singularity.descent-parity-average} with the total parity $\Gamma$ in place of its single-mode $\sigma$ (the form used in the stored theorem on the mode split), sends them to $0$; $E(p_{k}) = p_{k}$; the averaged CHSH element is $2c\,p_{1}p_{2}$, of value $2c$. The last statement is (ii) applied to either party: in the twisted split the observables of $B'$ are $\pm 1$ and $tp_{2} + u\,e_{2}p_{1}$ by the isomorphism $B' \cong \Cl(1,1)$, even exactly when $u = 0$.

\emph{(v).} $e_{1}e_{2} = -e_{2}e_{1}$ and $(e_{1}e_{2})^{\dagger} = e_{2}e_{1} = -e_{1}e_{2}$. If $\varphi(x^{\dagger}) = \varphi(x)$ for all $x$ then $\varphi(e_{1}e_{2}) = -\varphi(e_{1}e_{2}) = 0$; for $\varphi = \langle\rho\,\cdot\,\rangle_{0}$ with $\rho^{\dagger} = \rho$ this holds because $\langle\rho x^{\dagger}\rangle_{0} = \langle(x\rho)^{\dagger}\rangle_{0} = \langle x\rho\rangle_{0} = \langle\rho x\rangle_{0}$. (Over real coefficients positivity alone does not give $\varphi(x^{\dagger}) = \varphi(x)$, which is why it is a hypothesis of the clause.) Put $X = e_{1}p_{2}$, $Y = p_{1}e_{2}$, $Z = p_{1}p_{2}$: each is a product of two commuting self-adjoint elements of square $1$, so is self-adjoint of square $1$, and $(e_{1}e_{2})$ is the only term of the untwisted element that is not self-adjoint, so its self-adjoint part is $H = X + Y - Z$. $XZ = e_{1}p_{1} = -p_{1}e_{1} = -ZX$, likewise $YZ = -ZY$, and $XY = e_{1}p_{1}\,p_{2}e_{2}$, $YX = p_{1}e_{2}e_{1}p_{2} = -p_{1}e_{1}\,e_{2}p_{2} = -XY$. So $H^{2} = 3$ and $\varphi(H)^{2} \le \varphi(H^{2}) = 3$ for every state.

check_py:
"""synthesis.chsh-with-parity-even-observables-needs-two-modes-per-party-and-no-klein-twist: exact checks.

Modes are the null pairs of Cl(l,l): generators e_k (square +1, index 2k) and f_k (square -1, index 2k+1),
mode parity p_k = f_k e_k, total parity Gamma = product of the p_k. The dagger sends a blade to its inverse.
An observable is self-adjoint of square one; it is even if it commutes with Gamma.

(1) even elements of disjoint mode sets commute with no twist, the twist does nothing to them, and the even
    observables of one mode are 1 and p only, so a one-mode party gives C^2 = 4;
(2) two modes per party: even observables with C^2 = 4 + 4K and even states with values 8r;
(3) one mode per party with the Klein twist: values 2(c + s) on the even pair state, but through observables
    that anticommute with the parity and are erased by the parity average; without the twist the odd
    observables anticommute and their product has value 0 in every state.
"""
from fractions import Fraction as F
from itertools import combinations

import GA
from tp_premise import premise

ONE = GA.sc(F(1))


def dsign(b, sq):
    g = len(b)
    s = (-1) ** (g * (g - 1) // 2)
    for i in b:
        s *= sq[i]
    return s


def dagger(x, sq):
    return {b: c * dsign(b, sq) for b, c in x.items()}


def prod(sq, *xs):
    r = ONE
    for x in xs:
        r = GA.mul(r, x, sq)
    return r


def comm(x, y, sq):
    return GA.sub(GA.mul(x, y, sq), GA.mul(y, x, sq))


def chsh(sq, a1, a2, b1, b2):
    return GA.add(prod(sq, a1, b1), prod(sq, a1, b2), prod(sq, a2, b1), GA.neg(prod(sq, a2, b2)))


def s0(x):
    return x.get((), F(0))


def modes(m):
    sq = tuple(s for _ in range(m) for s in (1, -1))
    e = [GA.gen(2 * k) for k in range(m)]
    f = [GA.gen(2 * k + 1) for k in range(m)]
    p = [GA.mul(f[k], e[k], sq) for k in range(m)]
    return sq, e, f, p, prod(sq, *p)


def is_obs(x, sq):
    return dagger(x, sq) == x and prod(sq, x, x) == ONE


def parity_average(x, gam, sq):
    return GA.scal(F(1, 2), GA.add(x, prod(sq, gam, x, gam)))


def check_even_observables_commute_without_twist_and_one_mode_has_only_the_parity():
    premise("synthesis.mode-split-of-the-clifford-algebra-and-its-klein-twist-to-the-tensor-product")
    premise("singularity.descent-parity-average")
    sq, e, f, p, gam = modes(3)
    # party A = mode 0, party B = modes 1, 2
    a_idx, b_idx = (0, 1), (2, 3, 4, 5)
    a_blades = [b for k in range(3) for b in combinations(a_idx, k)]
    b_blades = [b for k in range(5) for b in combinations(b_idx, k)]
    a_even = [b for b in a_blades if len(b) % 2 == 0]
    b_even = [b for b in b_blades if len(b) % 2 == 0]
    assert len(a_even) == 2 and len(b_even) == 8
    for a in a_even:
        for b in b_even:
            assert GA.commutes({a: F(1)}, {b: F(1)}, sq)
    assert GA.anticommutes(e[0], e[1], sq)
    # the twist by the parity of A does nothing to even elements of B
    tw = [prod(sq, y, p[0]) for y in (e[1], f[1], e[2], f[2])]
    un = [e[1], f[1], e[2], f[2]]
    for i, j in combinations(range(4), 2):
        assert prod(sq, tw[i], tw[j]) == prod(sq, un[i], un[j])
    # self-adjoint blades of one mode: 1, e, p; the even ones: 1, p
    herm = [b for b in a_blades if dsign(b, sq) == 1]
    assert herm == [(), (0,), (0, 1)]
    assert [b for b in herm if GA.commutes({b: F(1)}, gam, sq)] == [(), (0, 1)]
    x = GA.add(GA.scal(F(3, 5), p[0]), GA.scal(F(4, 5), e[0]))
    assert is_obs(x, sq) and not GA.commutes(x, gam, sq)
    assert parity_average(x, gam, sq) == GA.scal(F(3, 5), p[0])
    # a one-mode party with even observables against a two-mode party with non-commuting even observables
    b1, b2 = p[1], prod(sq, e[1], f[2])
    assert is_obs(b1, sq) and is_obs(b2, sq) and GA.anticommutes(b1, b2, sq)
    for a1, a2 in ((p[0], p[0]), (p[0], GA.neg(p[0])), (ONE, p[0])):
        c = chsh(sq, a1, a2, b1, b2)
        assert prod(sq, c, c) == GA.sc(F(4))
    return True


def check_two_modes_per_party_reach_square_eight_with_even_observables_and_even_states():
    premise("synthesis.mode-split-of-the-clifford-algebra-and-its-klein-twist-to-the-tensor-product")
    sq, e, f, p, gam = modes(4)
    a1, a2 = p[0], prod(sq, e[0], f[1])
    b1, b2 = p[2], prod(sq, e[2], f[3])
    for o in (a1, a2, b1, b2):
        assert is_obs(o, sq) and GA.commutes(o, gam, sq)
    assert GA.anticommutes(a1, a2, sq) and GA.anticommutes(b1, b2, sq)
    for a in (a1, a2):
        for b in (b1, b2):
            assert GA.commutes(a, b, sq)
    c = chsh(sq, a1, a2, b1, b2)
    k = GA.neg(prod(sq, f[0], f[1], f[2], f[3]))
    assert prod(sq, c, c) == GA.add(GA.sc(F(4)), GA.scal(F(4), k))
    assert is_obs(k, sq) and GA.commutes(k, c, sq) and GA.commutes(k, gam, sq)
    for r in (F(1, 3), F(239, 676)):
        assert 8 * r * r <= 1
        rho = prod(sq, GA.add(ONE, k), GA.add(ONE, GA.scal(r, c)))
        assert dagger(rho, sq) == rho and GA.commutes(rho, gam, sq)
        assert s0(rho) == 1 and s0(prod(sq, rho, c)) == 8 * r and s0(prod(sq, rho, c, c)) == 8
        assert 4 < (8 * r) ** 2 < 8
    return True


def check_twisted_one_mode_split_exceeds_two_only_through_odd_observables():
    premise("synthesis.mode-split-of-the-clifford-algebra-and-its-klein-twist-to-the-tensor-product")
    premise("singularity.descent-parity-average")
    sq, e, f, p, gam = modes(2)
    tw = prod(sq, e[1], p[0])
    for o in (p[0], e[0], p[1], tw):
        assert is_obs(o, sq)
    for a in (p[0], e[0]):
        for b in (p[1], tw):
            assert GA.commutes(a, b, sq)
    assert GA.anticommutes(p[0], e[0], sq) and GA.anticommutes(p[1], tw, sq)
    # the two observables the violation needs are odd: they anticommute with the parity and the average erases them
    for o in (e[0], tw):
        assert GA.anticommutes(o, gam, sq) and parity_average(o, gam, sq) == {}
    # the stored pair state at equal weights, an even pure state
    v = [GA.scal(F(1, 2), GA.add(e[k], f[k])) for k in range(2)]
    w = [GA.scal(F(1, 2), GA.sub(e[k], f[k])) for k in range(2)]
    rho = GA.add(GA.scal(F(1, 4), GA.add(ONE, prod(sq, p[0], p[1]))),
                 GA.scal(F(1, 2), GA.add(prod(sq, w[0], w[1]), prod(sq, v[1], v[0]))))
    assert dagger(rho, sq) == rho and prod(sq, rho, rho) == rho and GA.commutes(rho, gam, sq)
    val = lambda x: 4 * s0(prod(sq, rho, x))
    assert val(ONE) == 1
    assert [val(prod(sq, a, b)) for a in (p[0], e[0]) for b in (p[1], tw)] == [1, 0, 0, 1]
    for (cc, ss, expect) in ((F(3, 5), F(4, 5), F(14, 5)), (F(20, 29), F(21, 29), F(82, 29)),
                             (F(119, 169), F(120, 169), F(478, 169))):
        assert cc * cc + ss * ss == 1
        bp = GA.add(GA.scal(cc, p[1]), GA.scal(ss, tw))
        bm = GA.sub(GA.scal(cc, p[1]), GA.scal(ss, tw))
        assert is_obs(bp, sq) and is_obs(bm, sq)
        c = chsh(sq, p[0], e[0], bp, bm)
        assert val(c) == expect == 2 * (cc + ss) and 4 < expect * expect < 8
        # after the parity average of the observables the square of the CHSH element is 4
        ca = chsh(sq, p[0], parity_average(e[0], gam, sq), parity_average(bp, gam, sq), parity_average(bm, gam, sq))
        assert val(ca) == 2 * cc and val(ca) <= 2
    # without the twist: e_1 and e_2 anticommute, their product is anti-self-adjoint, and has value 0 in a state
    g = prod(sq, e[0], e[1])
    assert GA.anticommutes(e[0], e[1], sq) and dagger(g, sq) == GA.neg(g) and val(g) == 0
    cu = chsh(sq, e[0], p[0], e[1], p[1])
    h = GA.scal(F(1, 2), GA.add(cu, dagger(cu, sq)))
    assert h == GA.add(prod(sq, e[0], p[1]), prod(sq, p[0], e[1]), GA.neg(prod(sq, p[0], p[1])))
    assert prod(sq, h, h) == GA.sc(F(3))
    return True
